Rohan,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is the section of our RFI focused on IP, indemnity, and liability caps. We need to capture Redwood's positions in time for our legal review next week. High-level asks:

- Confirm whether Redwood proposes assignment, license, or retained ownership for model improvements and customer prompts.
- Proposed indemnity scope and any sublimits/exclusions (e.g., third-party model outputs).
- Liability cap approach and whether Redwood will accept higher caps tied to committed spend or order form schedules.
- Any optional exhibits/order forms we can sign to modify defaults.

Subject: Re: Aurora RFI: IP & Liability exhibits — initial questionnaire

Jane —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached is a first-pass completed worksheet (Aurora_RFI_IP_Answers_v1.xlsx) and a draft order form in PDF to show how caps/tiers could map to committed spend. High-level positions in this draft:

- Ownership: Redwood retains ownership of our platform and model variants; customers receive a broad license to outputs and any customer-provided content. We can discuss narrower assignment for customer-fed, non-derivative code artifacts but would need scope and compensation details.
- Indemnity: Redwood provides IP infringement indemnity for Redwood-delivered models (subject to exclusions for third-party model components and customer misuse).
- Liability cap: Default cap tied to fees paid in prior 12 months (greater of $1M or 12 months of fees) with an option to negotiate higher caps in a signed Exhibit on the order form.

We know Aurora is regulated — looping in Evelyn (legal) and Karthik (sales) to confirm if we should offer an elevated cap for PHI/regulated use under a special Exhibit Q.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the worksheet.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurora RFI: IP & Liability exhibits — initial questionnaire

Rohan —

Reviewed your draft answers. A few suggested edits and flags (summary below; see inline comments in the spreadsheet):

1) Ownership/Improvements:
- Do not accept automatic assignment for model improvements — recommend: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Data; Redwood retains ownership of platform, model weights, and system-level improvements. Any bespoke model tuning or IP explicitly developed and paid for by Customer may be treated as work-for-hire subject to a separate SOW."

2) Indemnity scope:
- Keep standard IP indemnity for Redwood-supplied models, but explicitly carve out: (a) outputs derived from third-party models not under Redwood's control; (b) prompts or data supplied by Customer that cause infringement.
- Add standard 'notification and cure' obligations then escalation to limitation of remedies.

3) Liability cap language:
- Your "greater of $1M or 12 months fees" is reasonable as a default. For regulated PHI use, recommend a separate Exhibit Q where we accept a higher negotiated cap tied to a multi-year commitment or reserved capacity (Dedicated).
- Avoid open-ended consequential damages waivers language — keep mutual limitation of liability with exceptions for gross negligence and willful misconduct.

4) Order form: Ensure the order form includes a clause where the "Order-Specific Commitment" can raise the cap in the SOW/Exhibit when both parties sign. This is how we avoid contract fragmentation and preserve negotiation levers.

If you want, I can draft redline text for Exhibit Q (data processing, extra-security obligations, and an alternate cap option).

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Lead Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Jane,

Thanks — attaching an updated worksheet that incorporates Redwood's legal suggestions and a draft "Exhibit Q — Regulated Data & Elevated Cap" (Exhibit-Q-Data-Processing-Draft.docx). Key updates:

- Ownership language clarified to reflect retention of Redwood platform/IP and license to customers for outputs; bespoke deliverables (e.g., fine-tuning paid for by Aurora) flagged as negotiable on a per-project basis.
- Indemnity: retained Redwood indemnity for Redwood-controlled model code; explicit carve-outs for third-party model components and for customer-supplied prompts.
- Liability cap: default remains greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months fees; included clear mechanism in the Order Form to raise cap by signed Exhibit/Order-Specific Commitment.

If Aurora prefers a deterministic cap tied to committed spend (example tiers in the attached order form), we can map the Exhibit to reserved capacity (Dedicated) or a longer-term commitment.

Would you like a short call Monday to walk counsel through Exhibit Q? We can provide a redline for your legal team to react to.

Regards,
Rohan

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Aurora RFI: IP & Liability exhibits — initial questionnaire

Rohan — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping in counsel. A few clarifying questions from our legal/regulatory side after a quick read-through:

1) Third-party models: Aurora runs a mix of open models and licensed third-party models. We need explicit language that delineates Redwood's responsibility if outputs generated by a combined pipeline infringe third-party rights. Your carve-out is a start, but counsel wants an approach for (a) where Redwood integrates third-party model plugins, and (b) where Aurora configures models in its environment using Redwood tooling.

2) PHI/regulation: For regulated PHI workloads, our security team will require a clear SLA and higher liability cap tied to Dedicated capacity or an Enterprise deployment. Can Exhibit Q include sample dollar figures (e.g., $5M cap for >$X committed spend) so procurement can see feasibility?

3) Order form: your tiered mapping looks promising. Will Redwood accept language where a signed Order specifically amends the default liability cap to the higher tier? Our counsel prefers explicit amendment language versus referencing a separate Exhibit.

Can we get proposed redline snippets for (1) third-party model carve-out resolution and (2) sample Exhibit dollar figures? If so, let's schedule a 30-min call Monday 10am PT.

Best,
Jane
Jane Smith
Senior Sourcing Manager
Aurora Health Systems

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Aurora RFI: IP & Liability exhibits — initial questionnaire

Jane —

Thanks for the questions. Evelyn and I drafted two concise options below to present on Monday; I attached the Exhibit Q draft and a redline snippet for the Order Form amendment language. High-level options: 

Option A — Standard Order Form amendment (preferred for speed):
- "Order-Specific Amendment: The parties agree that the Order Form signed by Customer may expressly amend Section [Liability Cap] of the Agreement to set a higher liability cap as set forth in the Order. Such amendment will apply only to the Services and period specified in the Order."
- Typical example: "Cap for Order AUR-2026-07 = greater of $5,000,000 or 18 months fees (for Dedicated capacity committed at $X/month)."

Option B — Exhibit Q (for regulated PHI or multi-year Reserved capacity):
- Exhibit Q includes: data processing addendum, enhanced security controls, audit rights, and an explicit higher-cap table tied to committed spend tiers (sample figures included in Exhibit Q: $3M / $5M / $10M for defined commitment bands).

Third-party model carve-out proposal (redline snippet):
- "Redwood liability and indemnity obligations shall not extend to claims arising from (i) third-party model components licensed or otherwise incorporated into the Services by Customer or by Customer's authorized integrators, or (ii) Customer configurations or prompt engineering that materially alter model outputs. Where Redwood actively manages and integrates a third-party model on behalf of Customer under a documented integration statement of work, Redwood will assume responsibility for infringement claims solely to the extent such claims arise from Redwood's integration work and not from third-party licensor terms."

Next steps: Evelyn will bring the redline to the call; can you confirm Monday 10:00 AM PT? If that works, we'll send a calendar invite and a one-page comparison doc so your counsel can orient quickly.

Appreciate the partnership — want to get you a defensible path for PHI workloads without blocking procurement schedules.

Best regards,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Exhibit-Q-Data-Processing-Draft.docx; OrderForm-Amendment-Redline.pdf
